question: Does the identity-qualified R137b selector remain within 3% of natural oneDNN through c64 when control and candidate are measured in an interleaved same-session A-B-B-A design?
basis: R137b passed all 3,072 dense shape/M identity pairs. Its c64 ratio against the older R135 control was 1.032844, only 0.002844 above the gate and inconsistent with R136's 1.016875 same-session model, so a paired drift-resistant measurement is required before serving integration.
aggregation: For each shape and arm, take the median of the two independent run medians at each M; multiply by the production call counts and sum; divide B by A.

gates.decode: The paired weighted B/A ratio must be <=1.03 independently at M2, M4, M8, M16, M32, M64, and M128.
gates.prefill: Report M168 and M256; either ratio above 2.00 rejects serving integration.
gates.stability: No arm may have a timing sample max/min ratio above 1.15 at M128; otherwise the affected shape is rerun once under a separately recorded amendment.
gates.health: No new Xe fault, copy-engine fault, CAT error, reset, timeout, hang, coredump, or device loss.
gates.on_pass: Record R138 and preregister the first serving-compatible R137b package and endpoint gate.
gates.on_failure: Keep R137b as an exact reference only and optimize the wide fixed-K strategy before any server build.
